body:
Context:
Redwood's unified rollouts support multiple rollout strategies (canary, A/B, shadow) with automated rollback based on SLOs and per-metric thresholds. Customers have asked for two practical additions that improve emergency handling and reduce noisy rollbacks: a manual quarantine action (operator-initiated pause + isolate traffic) and a metric-quorum evaluation mode (require X of N metrics to cross thresholds before triggering auto-rollback).

Motivation:
- Manual quarantine lets SREs/operators immediately stop progressive exposure when they see suspicious signals, isolate the candidate variant, and continue investigation without a full rollback. This is useful for noisy but non-critical metric anomalies or when debugging reproductions with limited traffic.
- Metric-quorum reduces sensitivity to single-metric noise: instead of OR/AND across metrics, teams can define how many metrics must fire to trigger an auto-rollback. This reduces false positives for autorollback in multi-metric policies.

What I changed (high level):
- Controller: added a QuarantineController to accept manual quarantine actions via API, update rollout state machine (Quarantined, QuarantineInvestigating), and expose TTL/release hooks so automated systems can still resume when cleared.
- Evaluator: implemented MetricQuorumEvaluator which takes a list of metric evaluations and a quorum threshold (e.g. 2-of-3) and produces a single decision used by the autorollback engine. Backwards compatible with existing AND/OR semantics.
- API: extended rollout proto and REST shape with optional fields: "quarantine_action" and "metric_quorum_threshold". Existing rollout specs without these fields are unchanged.
- UI/CLI: added a manual "Quarantine" button on rollout detail pages (with required justification modal) and `redwood rollouts quarantine <id> --reason` CLI command. Actions are auditable with operator identity and linked tickets.
- Observability: added dashboard panels and spans for quarantine events, quorum voting breakdown, and rollback decision timelines.
- Tests: unit tests for quorum evaluator, controller state transitions, and e2e scenarios covering canary+shadow with manual quarantine and quorum-triggered rollback.

Rollout policy examples (docs included):
- automatic_quorum_example.yaml: metric_quorum_threshold: 2
  metrics:
    - latency_p50 > 300ms
    - error_rate > 1%
    - model_quality_regression > 0.02
  This triggers autorollback only if at least 2 of the 3 metrics cross their thresholds within the evaluation window.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Existing rollout specs continue to behave as before. The API additions are optional. The controller will ignore unknown fields from older clients.
- For private deployments, we added migration notes in docs/manual_quarantine.md outlining the DB migration (small schema delta to store quarantine events). The migration is non-blocking and includes a safety flag so operators can opt-in.

Testing and QA:
- Unit test coverage for quorum evaluator + controller state machine.
- E2E: two e2e scenarios added: 1) staged-canary with metric noise where quorum prevents rollback; 2) manual quarantine workflow where operator quarantines a canary, confirms traffic isolation, and later either resumes or rolls back.
- CI: reran flaky e2e once; added retry with exponential backoff for known timing flakiness in canary traffic simulation.

Security and audit:
- Manual quarantine action requires `rollouts.quarantine` permission in RBAC. Actions are logged to audit-log and exposed to the console.

Usage notes for operators:
- Use the quarantine button to isolate pacing traffic while investigating. Provide justification; the UI links to recent alerts and traces to speed triage.
- Set metric-quorum conservatively (e.g., 2-of-3) and tune per-workload.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Add auto-unquarantine heuristics (TTL + anomaly-cleared detection) — tracked in ENG-4922.
- More granular traffic mirroring while quarantined for reproductions — tracked in PM-389.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller + evaluator implementation
- [x] API proto + REST mapping
- [x] UI + CLI surface
- [x] Unit and e2e tests
- [x] Docs and migration notes
- [x] Observability dashboards

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on the controller state transitions (quarantine -> investigating -> resume/rollback) and the quorum evaluation math (threshold semantics and windowing). The quorum evaluator is intentionally small and isolated to keep reasoning simple.
- The proto change is additive; reviewers should check the REST serializer for correct optional handling.

References:
- Linear: ENG-4821 (design), ENG-4922 (follow-up auto-unquarantine), PM-331 (customer request)
review_comments: Carlos Ruiz: Left a few comments on the controller state machine — prefer explicit tombstone vs TTL-only for quarantine events to make audit easier.
Aisha Patel (author): Addressed tombstone suggestion, added TTL + tombstone flag so we keep explicit operator-initiated quarantine records. Updated tests to assert tombstone presence.
Evelyn Zhang: Quorum evaluator looks good, but please add a test for metric evaluation windows crossing boundary (partial windows).
Aisha Patel: Added window-boundary test and a comment explaining sliding-window semantics. Also included a note in docs explaining tuning tradeoffs.
Tomoko Sato: Found a race between evaluator result and rollback trigger; added a small lock in controller and a test to reproduce — fixed and validated.
Carlos Ruiz: Approve after addressing comments.
